summary: During the scheduling run, a total of 1281 passes were observed, with 289 (22.6%) being scheduled. A significant number, 992 (77.4%), were dropped, with 60 of these being priority-1 passes. Among the dropped passes, 694 had alternatives, while 298 did not. The median delay to an alternative for those without one was 383.6 minutes. This indicates a high drop rate, with a substantial number of priority-passes also being missed, and a considerable portion of these drops lacking timely alternatives.
